findings.issue: toThrow(new RangeError(message)) asserts only the message, not the error class, so an implementation that throws a plain Error with the same text would still pass. The spec requires RangeError.
findings.evidence: Vitest/Jest toThrow(errorInstance) compares only .message. Lines 40 and 49 use this form.
findings.fix: Also assert the class, e.g. expect(() => ...).toThrow(RangeError) next to the message check, or use a thrown-error capture plus expect(err).toBeInstanceOf(RangeError).

findings.issue: The match case asserts only ruleId 'match', not grade 'correct'. The alternative case on the next line asserts both.
A-2 says equityPct is checked before requiredEquityPct, but no case makes both non-finite, so the order is never exercised.
findings.evidence: Each case sets only one field to a non-finite value.
findings.fix: Optionally add one case with both fields NaN that expects the equityPct message.

summary: The implementation matches the spec. finitePct guards only the fields the deciding margin rule reads: equityPct before requiredEquityPct in the call-fold rule, and equityVsCallingRangePct after the undefined/null early return in the aggression rule. The value === undefined check is needed for TypeScript narrowing because Number.isFinite is not a type guard. Finite inputs follow the same path as before, so their grades are unchanged. The locked tests/advice/grade.acceptance.test.ts has no diff against main. The tests/advice/grade.test.ts diff renames one test and adds expect(26.7 - 16.7).toBe(10), with no removed expect lines. The -15 test would fail against a Math.abs mutant (it would return major/15). The grader and table suites pass (17 files, 75 tests), and the gates pass (test, lint, typecheck, scope 111/120 lines, 3/3 files). No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
